title: Hello Digit redress moves from automated-savings enforcement to a dated payment-notification stage
source_unit: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Hello Digit enforcement and payment-administration record
geography: United States; CFPB enforcement and Civil Penalty Fund administration

minimum_consumer_redress.unit: USD; minimum redress required for the overdraft-fee representation violation

observations.method: Transcribed from the CFPB's official payment-by-case page. The record separates the consent-order obligation and administration route from later notification, payment delivery, receipt, and adequacy.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not identify the eligible-recipient denominator, individual allocation, payment method, amount per person, account correction, or later financial outcome.
observations.subgroup: Consumers covered by the CFPB's Hello Digit redress provision; the public record does not publish a stable recipient key.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal redress obligation and administrator can create a reachable remedy route without proving that eligible consumers were identified, paid, or made whole.

payment_receipt_verified.unit: recipient-level payment receipt located in the public case record

recipient_allocation_published.unit: recipient-level allocation or stable recipient key published in the public case record

observations.method: Transcribed from the CFPB's current Hello Digit case page, last modified October 15, 2026. The dated email notification is treated as an administration checkpoint, not as payment delivery or acceptance.
observations.uncertainty: The page does not state the number of notified recipients, email delivery success, payment date, payment method, individual amount, returned payments, recipient acceptance, or later household recovery.
observations.subgroup: Potentially eligible Hello Digit consumers contacted through the EPIQ-administered redress route.
observations.counterinterpretation: Notification can be a necessary step toward payment while still leaving delivery, acceptance, adequacy, and account correction unresolved.

denominator.unit: CFPB Civil Penalty Fund allocation entry for Hello Digit

allocated_amount.unit: USD; CFPB-listed allocation to eligible Hello Digit victims

recipient_payment_receipt_verified.unit: recipient-level payment receipt or acceptance record located in the public allocation page

account_correction_verified.unit: recipient account correction or residual-loss record located in the public allocation page

observations.method: Transcribed from the CFPB Civil Penalty Fund page, which lists $38,220 allocated to Hello Digit. The allocation is kept separate from the $68,145 minimum redress obligation, notification, payment delivery, and recipient receipt.
observations.uncertainty: The public allocation entry does not identify recipient count, individual amounts, payment date, delivery channel, returned payments, acceptance, adequacy, account correction, or later household outcome.
observations.subgroup: Eligible Hello Digit victims within the CFPB Civil Penalty Fund allocation; no stable recipient key is public.
observations.counterinterpretation: An agency allocation demonstrates a funding stage but does not establish that the allocated money reached eligible consumers or resolved the underlying overdraft harm.

denominator.unit: EPIQ Hello Digit administrator public website

public_site_http_status.unit: HTTP response code from a public fetch

separate_payment_status_page_located.unit: separate public payment-status page located in the bounded web/search check

observations.method: Bounded read-only access check of the CFPB-linked administrator domain and exact-domain web search. The result records a technical/public-access boundary, not payment nonoccurrence.
observations.uncertainty: A 403 response may reflect bot protection, access controls, or site configuration; it cannot establish whether payments were sent, accepted, returned, or corrected. A private recipient portal or administrator response may contain fields not publicly indexed.
observations.subgroup: Potential Hello Digit redress recipients and other parties seeking payment-status information through the EPIQ administrator route.
observations.counterinterpretation: An inaccessible public site can coexist with an active payment process; non-observation here is an acquisition limitation rather than evidence of nonpayment.

related_sources.claim: The CFPB lists Hello Digit among ongoing cases and distinguishes Bureau-administered and Civil Penalty Fund compensation routes.
The CFPB identifies this as the EPIQ administrator website; a bounded public fetch on 2026-10-19 returned HTTP 403, so no public payment-status content was acquired.

boundary: This record follows a named automated-savings enforcement case through a formal redress obligation and dated payment-notification stage. It does not establish recipient-level payment receipt, adequacy, account correction, repeat exposure, trust, continued use, switching, or exit.
